title: TasteProfile
description: The user's taste preferences, collected by the first-launch wizard and editable from Settings. PERSISTED AS JSON: Swift encodes it with JSONEncoder and stores the blob in UserDefaults under the key "tasteProfile" (TasteProfile.swift:38-49), so unlike the SwiftData models this schema IS the real on-disk shape. Source of record: DinnerDecider/Models/TasteProfile.swift:8-34. Each category is a list of tapped pills plus a free-text "other" field.

allergies.description: SAFETY-RELEVANT. Rendered as "Allergies: X. Never include these." in the prompt fragment.

spiceLevel.description: 1 (mild) to 5 (bring it on); 3 is the default. Values outside 1-5 fall back to the "medium spice" wording rather than erroring. The spice line is ALWAYS emitted in the prompt fragment, even for an otherwise-empty profile.

$comment:
Every key is listed as required because Swift's synthesized Decodable init does NOT fall back to a property's default value for a missing key on a non-optional property: a blob written by an older/partial writer fails to decode entirely, and `TasteProfile.load()` returns nil (try? swallows the error), silently losing the profile including allergies. A port that tolerates missing keys is more forgiving than iOS, which is safe in the direction that matters; a port that WRITES partial blobs would break iOS. Always write all 13 keys. The `hasContent` gate (any of the 6 pill lists non-empty, OR any of the 6 other-fields non-blank after trimming) decides whether the profile reaches the prompt at all - see shared/prompts/recipes.md.

SECOND TRAP, same consequence, different cause (found porting to Go, Sept 14 2026): the six list properties are `"type": "array"`, so JSON `null` is a schema violation, AND Swift decodes them into non-optional `[String]`, so a null fails the synthesized Decodable init exactly as a missing key does -- the whole profile is lost, allergies included. This matters because in Go a nil slice marshals to `null`, not `[]`. A Go writer that never initializes the six lists produces a blob that passes its own round-trip and is unreadable by iOS. Every writer MUST emit `[]` for an empty list, never null. Test it with a zero-value struct, which is the case that gets this wrong.
